results.name: inKind’s $414M Financing Surpasses $1.2B in Capital Raised
results.content:
inKind raises $414 million in financing led by Citi and Cross River, bringing total capital raised above $1.2 billion to expand its restaurant growth platform.
The oversubscribed second financing tranche includes $175 million from Citi and $150 million from Cross River in senior financing. Additional mezzanine financing includes $50 million from Sagard, $25 million from Varadero Capital and $14 million from Trinity Capital. The latest financing comes as inKind continues scaling a business model designed to connect restaurants with capital, technology and new customers.
inKind raises $414 million in financing led by Citi and Cross River, bringing total capital raised above $1.2 billion to expand its restaurant growth platform.
Today, the inKind restaurant network connects more than 5 million diners with more than 8,500 restaurants representing nearly $30 billion in annual restaurant gross merchandise value, or GMV. The $414 million financing follows a recently announced $320 million commitment from Liberty Mutual Investments, which is participating as a senior anchor and mezzanine lender.
Unlike traditional debt financing, which can create ongoing repayment obligations, or equity financing that can dilute an owner’s stake, inKind provides restaurants with upfront capital while also helping generate customer demand through its dining network.

results.name: inKind raises $414M financing led by Citi, Cross River | Value Add Pulse
results.content:
inKind, an Austin-based restaurant commerce platform, closed an oversubscribed $414 million financing tranche led by Citi and Cross River, pushing its total capital raised past $1.2 billion.
inKind announced the close of an oversubscribed $414 million second financing tranche on August 10, led by Citi and Cross River alongside Sagard, Varadero Capital and Trinity Capital, pushing the Austin-based company's total capital raised past $1.2 billion, according to PYMNTS and a company release.
The lead investors here -- Citi and Cross River -- are banks, not venture funds, which fits the nature of the raise: this is largely debt-like financing capital inKind deploys to restaurants, not equity funding a typical product roadmap.
Watch whether inKind discloses restaurant-level default rates in future raises -- that's the number that actually tells you whether $1.2 billion in cumulative financing is building a durable credit book or accumulating risk faster than the model can absorb it.
inKind's pitch to restaurants is unusual: it fronts capital to independent restaurants in exchange for future dining credit, which it then sells to consumers at a discount -- functioning less like a typical venture-backed startup and more like a structured-finance vehicle wrapped in a consumer app.

results.name: inKind Secures $414 Million Financing, Bringing Total Capital Raised Above $1.2 Billion
results.content:
inKind has closed an oversubscribed $414 million second financing tranche led by Citi and Cross River, bringing the restaurant commerce platform’s total capital raised to more than $1.2 billion.  
The financing includes $175 million from Citi and $150 million from Cross River at the senior level, along with $50 million from Sagard, $25 million from Varadero Capital and $14 million from Trinity Capital in mezzanine financing.  
The closing follows a recently announced $320 million commitment from Liberty Mutual Investments as a senior anchor and mezzanine lender. With the expanded facility, inKind plans to deploy more than $1 billion in growth capital to nearly 10,000 restaurants over the next year.  
Citi’s participation also expands an existing relationship with inKind, following a 2025 investment by Citi Ventures.  
inKind operates a restaurant commerce platform that combines upfront capital, demand generation, financial tools, guest rewards, proprietary data and AI-native capabilities. Its network currently connects more than 5 million diners with more than 8,500 restaurants representing nearly $30 billion in annual restaurant gross merchandise value.  
The company has expanded from approximately 1,000 restaurant partners in 2022 to more than 8,500 today. Its user base has also increased from roughly 1 million in March 2024 to more than 5 million.
inKind has provided more than $850 million in growth capital to restaurant partners and delivered more than $225 million in dining rewards to guests. Its restaurant partners include MINA Group, Ethan Stowell Restaurants, José Andrés Group, Okàn, Kann and Superiority Burger.  
**KEY QUOTES:**  
*“For more than a decade, inKind has been building a new way to finance and grow great restaurants.”*  
*“The addition of Citi, a global systemically important bank, is an important signal that the market increasingly recognizes the strength of the inKind model. This financing gives us the capacity to scale the restaurant commerce infrastructure we have spent more than a decade building.”*  
*“We believe inKind is still in the early chapters of what it can become. As our restaurant network grows, we can give more great operators access to millions of guests. As our guest base grows, we can give more diners access to the best restaurants in the country.”*  
**Johann Moonesinghe, Co-Founder and CEO of inKind**

results.content:
inKind closed an oversubscribed $414 million second financing tranche, with $175 million in senior capital from Citi and $150 million from Cross River, plus mezzanine financing of $50 million from Sagard, $25 million from Varadero Capital, and ...
inKind, which funds restaurants by buying their food-and-beverage credit at a discount, raised $414 million to pass $1.2 billion in total capital, with Citi taking senior position. Repaid in meals rather than interest or equity, the model sits alongside revenue-based financiers like Pipe and Clearco in the business of selling future revenue.
inKind closed an oversubscribed $414 million second financing tranche, with $175 million in senior capital from Citi and $150 million from Cross River, plus mezzanine financing of $50 million from Sagard, $25 million from Varadero Capital, and $14 million from Trinity Capital.
It’s why the industry views inKind as structurally closer to a prepaid gift-card business than to restaurant-tech SaaS. A step away sits revenue-based financing: Pipe, the “Nasdaq of revenue,” which sells SaaS contract revenue to investors at a discount; Capchase, which advances from its own balance sheet; and Clearco, which has funded more than 10,000 e-commerce companies with “equity-free capital.” But all of them are repaid in cash.
A globally systemic bank putting $175 million of senior capital behind an asset as unusual as food-and-beverage credit means the structure has passed institutional underwriting. Whether it becomes the standard filler for the gap between bank loans and equity in small-business finance is what inKind’s next year will test.
